Infobox 'Established: 1320'; the Tumanurung entry is dated 1300; the page itself says 'Not much is known about the exact time when the kingdom was established'. Same outline as 1512 for 1662-1669 (2,613 km2; the Gowa page has no area). Only Jum Pandan (ceded 1667) and the Somba Opu coast (1669) leave the outline; the new keyframes carry the rest to 1911.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the vassal sultanate, 1669-1911. The Makassar War page: Speelman 'destroyed the Somba Opu fortress and built Fort Rotterdam in its place as the headquarters of VOC activities in Sulawesi'; Palakka and the VOC divided power ('Palakka dominating internal affairs and the VOC dominating external affairs'). The Gowa page: 'In 1911 the Sultanate lost its independence ... and became one of the Dutch Indies' regencies'. The outline is the 1662 one minus the Makassar and Somba Opu cells (3 of 5 cells remain, about 1,570 km2); Kalegowa, the seat from 1670, lies in the Somba Opu cell, which a 10 km grid cannot separate from the fortress, so the capital dot sits on a cell the VOC took. The pages give no other change of extent before 1911.

region.text: Gowa and Tallo around Tamalate and Somba Opu on the Makassar coast

ledger.note: 1320: Gowa is established on the Makassar coast. Infobox 'Established: 1320' (Tumanurung dated 1300); 'Not much is known about the exact time when the kingdom was established'. Re-checked 2026-10-19: the Tallo Kingdom page gives no date for Gowa either (Tallo 'dates from the mid-15th century').

region.text: Tallo, on the coast north of Gowa

ledger.note: c. 1512: Gowa and Tallo are reunified. 'During the reign of King of Gowa X, Tunipalangga (1512-1546), the two kingdoms were reunified'; the page gives a reign span, not a year, so the year is Cliopatria's first (1512). Disagreement: the Tallo Kingdom page (opened 2026-10-19) puts the Gowa-Tallo power-sharing agreement 'during the reign of the 10th King of Gowa, Tunipalangga Ulaweng, and the 4th King of Tallo, Daeng Padulu' (c. 1540-1576), has Tallo founded in the mid-15th century and says nothing of 1512 or a merger year; the year stays Cliopatria's first (confidence 1).
1548: the capital moves from Tamalate to the fortress of Somba Opu (infobox: Tamalate 1320-1548, Somba Opu 1548-1670).
22 September 1605: Gowa-Tallo becomes a sultanate. 'The conversion of Tallo-Gowa to Islam is traditionally dated to September 22, 1605' (Sultan Alauddin reigned 1593-1639).

1611: Gowa invades Bone. 'Bone was invaded by the Sultanate of Gowa and pressured to convert to Islam.' Mirrors the Bone dossier's contest of 1611. The page does not call Bone a vassal; the vassalage is dated from 1646 (see below).

1611: Bone accepts Islam, 'the last major Bugis kingdom to accept Islam, in 1611' (Bone page); 'By 1611 all southwest Sulawesi, including Makassar's Bugis rival Bone, had become Muslim' (Gowa page). Closed the same year, as in the Bone dossier.

1618: Makassar attacks Sumbawa. 'Sumbawa was attacked through three expeditions in 1618, 1619, and 1626.' (Gowa page: 'In 1618 Makassar undertook the first of several attacks on the island of Sumbawa.')

1626: the third expedition. 'Salisi successfully resisted the Makassarese forces for a while, but was eventually defeated by a fleet from Sulawesi'; the page gives no year for the defeat, so the contest is closed at the last dated expedition (bridged).

1626: Sumbawa under Makassar. A rebellion 'against his Makassarese-backed rule took place in 1632-33, but was beaten down by troops from Sulawesi', and Bima had signed 'a contract of alliance with Makassar'; the page gives no tribute and no start year, so the vassalage is dated from the last expedition (bridged, confidence 1). Selayar, Buton, Lombok, Wajo, Soppeng and Luwu are still not on any page opened.
1644: Bone rises against Gowa. 'In 1644, Bone rose up against Gowa.' Mirrors the Bone dossier.

April-May 1646: Bone is defeated at Passempe. The page's footnote: 'the correct timeframe, according to the Makassar Annals, is 18 April-25 May 1646' (Andaya's 1644 is wrong). The Bone dossier closes the rising in 1645 (its bridging judgment); this page dates the battle a year later.

1646: Gowa installs a regent over Bone. After Passempe, Gowa put in 'a regent heading an Islamic religious council'; Bone is Gowa's vassal until 1667. Moved from 1611: the Bone page records only an invasion and a forced conversion in 1611, and mentions no vassalage. The Bone dossier (not changed here) has contests but no vassal pair.
1660: a Bugis revolt. 'In 1660 Arung Palakka, the long-haired prince of the Sultanate of Bone, led a Bugis revolt against Gowa.' Mirrors the Bone dossier.
1660: the revolt is 'ultimately crushed' and Palakka flees South Sulawesi; the page gives no month, so the contest is closed the same year.
1666: the Makassar War begins. 'the war later broke in 1666 between the VOC and the sultanate of Gowa'; the VOC expedition under Speelman sailed on 24 November 1666 (Makassar War page).
1667: Bone escapes Gowa. The Bone page's rulers' table restores La Maqdaremmeng in 1667 (1667-1672); Arung Palakka's Bugis fought with the VOC against Gowa (Makassar War page).

1667: Makassar loses Sumbawa. 'During the reign of Abu'l-Khair Sirajuddin the Makassar empire was soundly defeated by the Dutch East India Company (VOC) in 1667 and again in 1669. As a consequence the Makassarese formally lost their vast possessions in eastern Indonesia, including their suzerainty over Sumbawa.' The pages do not say who took Sumbawa.

18 November 1667: Gowa becomes a vassal of the VOC. 'On 18 November 1667, the Treaty of Bongaya was signed between Gowa and the VOC.' 'Gowa was reduced to a vassal of the VOC.' Here Gowa is the vassal and the VOC (booked under dutch-republic) the suzerain; the VOC's own dossier should carry the mirror.

region.text: Jum Pandan (Ujung Pandang), the fort converted into Fort Rotterdam

ledger.note: 18 November 1667: the Treaty of Bongaya cedes Jum Pandan to the VOC. 'Jum Pandan, a stronghold that would be converted into Fort Rotterdam, was ceded to the Dutch'; 'Gowa was reduced to a vassal of the VOC'; Hasanuddin had to destroy all fortresses but Somba Opu. Gowa's dependencies 'such as Minahasa, were transferred to the Netherlands' (undated before then, so no vassal_start).

June 1669: Somba Opu falls. 'allowing it to break the Sultanate of Gowa's strongest fortress in Somba Opu on June 12, 1669' (Makassar War page: the assault began 14 June and the fortress was abandoned about 22 June).

region.text: Somba Opu, the fortress that Speelman destroyed in June 1669, and the coast round it

ledger.note: June 1669: the VOC takes the Somba Opu coast. Speelman 'destroyed the Somba Opu fortress and built Fort Rotterdam in its place as the headquarters of VOC activities in Sulawesi'; 'Bone replaced Gowa as the supreme principality in South Sulawesi'. The page does not say how much land passed; one 10 km cell (with the Fort Rotterdam cell of 1667) is the researcher's reading, and the sultanate itself stays as a VOC vassal. Replaces the earlier loss of the whole core, which no page supports.
1670: the seat moves from Somba Opu to Kalegowa (infobox: Kalegowa 1670-1680, 1692-1702 and 1753-1895; Hasanuddin resigned in 1669 and died on 12 June 1670).

ledger.note: 1911: the Sultanate of Gowa ends as a state. The independent sultanate ended with Somba Opu in June 1669 (vassal from the Treaty of Bongaya, 18 November 1667); the formal sultanate lingered to 1945 and 1957 (the page's own dates).

wars.name: Makassar War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Bongaya (18 November 1667) reduced Gowa to a VOC vassal and ceded Jum Pandan; Hasanuddin renewed the war and lost Somba Opu in June 1669; Bone, with the VOC, replaced Gowa as the leading South Sulawesi state.
wars.note: The Makassar War page gives the war as 24 November 1666 to 24 June 1669, VOC-Bugis victory on 12 October 1668 and Somba Opu abandoned about 22 June 1669; the Gowa page has 12 June 1669. After 1669 Palakka and the VOC 'arranged a division of power, with Palakka dominating internal affairs and the VOC dominating external affairs'.

wars.name: Gowa's expeditions against Sumbawa
wars.outcome: Three expeditions (1618, 1619, 1626) overcame Salisi's resistance; a Makassarese-backed ruler was installed and a rebellion of 1632-33 was beaten down; suzerainty over Sumbawa ended with the VOC's victories of 1667/1669.
wars.note: Gowa page: 'In 1618 Makassar undertook the first of several attacks on the island of Sumbawa.' No year for the final defeat.

wars.name: Gowa's wars with Bone
wars.outcome: Gowa invaded Bone in 1611 and forced its conversion; Bone rose in 1644 and was defeated at Passempe (April-May 1646), after which Gowa installed a regent; the Bugis revolt of 1660 under Arung Palakka was crushed; Bone's king was restored in 1667.
wars.note: The 1611 invasion is from the Bone page; the Bone dossier (not changed) dates the end of the 1644 rising 1645.

notes: Cliopatria 'Sultanate of Gowa' (2 shapes, 1512..1669, 2,613 km2, identical outlines 1512-1661 and 1662-1669). Both shapes are the Gowa-Tallo core and are verdict ok; the infobox gives no area. (1) Start: the infobox says 'Established 1320' and the page admits the date is unknown; Cliopatria begins 1512, so a keyframe 1320-1511 carries the core back (confidence 1). (2) End: REPAIRED. The sovereign sultanate ends in June 1669 (Somba Opu) but is a VOC vassal from 18 November 1667 and survives to 1911, when 'the Sultanate lost its independence ... and became one of the Dutch Indies' regencies'; the page's 1945 (dissolved) and 1957 (infobox) are formal dates after that. The dossier ends in 1911, with vassal events for the VOC (to 31 December 1799) and the Dutch East Indies (1800-1911). (3) Dependencies are not in the shape: Bone (vassal 1646-1667; contests 1611, 1644-1646, 1660), Sumbawa (first attack 1618; the page gives neither conquest nor tribute), Minahasa (transferred to the Netherlands in 1667, undated before). Selayar, Buton, Lombok, Wajo, Soppeng and Luwu are not on the pages opened. Gowa's later conquest of Lombok and West Sumbawa, which overlaps Cliopatria's Balinese Kingdom shape of 1609-1682, is not on any page opened either (see the balinese-kingdom dossier). (4) Pages disagree on Somba Opu: 12 June 1669 (Gowa page) against an assault from 14 June and an abandonment on about 22 June (Makassar War page; infobox ends 24 June 1669). (5) 'Tallo' is a counterpart without a dossier (suggested slug kingdom-of-tallo). Page budget 1-2: four pages were opened because Bone and the Makassar War pages were the counterpart's. The fetch tool returns a model summary of each page; quotation marks mean 'as the fetched text gave it'. REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review): the 1669 loss of the whole core and the successor dutch-republic are gone; only the Fort Rotterdam cell (1667) and the Somba Opu cell (1669) leave the outline; keyframes 1668 and 1669-1911 carry it; successor dutch-east-indies. Bone: the vassalage moves from 1611 to 1646 (the Bone page records only an invasion and forced conversion in 1611; the Makassar War page has Passempe in April-May 1646 and a Gowa regent) and the Gowa ledger now mirrors the Bone dossier's contests (1611, 1644-1646, 1660). The Bone dossier (verdict fix, not touched) still lacks the vassal pair 1646-1667 with sultanate-of-gowa and ends its 1644 rising in 1645, a year before Passempe; the Bone tint of 1669-1814 over 'South Sulawesi principalities' should exclude Gowa's land, which is a VOC vassal. Sumbawa: the Bima page dates three expeditions (1618, 1619, 1626) and a rebellion of 1632-33; the vassalage 1626-1667 is bridged (confidence 1). Tallo: the page gives no merger year. Capital: Kalegowa in three periods (infobox), seats between them unknown. Rulers 17-33 from the table, except the garbled 1739-1742 rows. Pages not opened for Selayar, Buton, eastern Lombok and Minahasa.
